safety_verdicts.content: There has been no bleeding, discharge, or spread of the rash.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not address bleeding, discharge, or lack of spread.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting whether there is bleeding/discharge or whether the rash is spreading reduces the ability to distinguish uncomplicated eczema from infected dermatitis or other evolving rashes. This mainly risks delayed recognition/escalation if secondary infection or rapid progression were present.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient is systemically well, denying any fevers, vomiting, shortness of breath, cough, or bowel symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated only includes denial of fever and does not cover vomiting, SOB/cough, or bowel symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting key systemic review (vomiting, shortness of breath/cough, bowel symptoms) weakens documentation that the patient is systemically well, which is important when evaluating diffuse pruritic rashes and excluding red-flag infection or allergic/systemic illness. This can contribute to missed deterioration cues and suboptimal safety-netting.

This may lead to inappropriate management choices or mis-triage in subsequent encounters relying on the note.

While not immediately life-threatening, it can cause avoidable changes in evaluation or therapy.
